identification.title: Abide
identification.notes: Written by Aaron Williams with Aaron Keyes and Jake Fauber. CCLI 7168160. Has since reached the CCLI US Top 100; a 2024 version features Jon Reddick.

claims.structuralNotes: Three verses over a chorus that expands on its second and third returns, with a closing tag. Built on the vine and branches, with the singer's dependence as the running theme.

claims.claim: The singer can do nothing apart from Christ.
claims.subject: Dependence

claims.claim: The singer asks to be drawn close and taught to abide.
claims.subject: Abiding

claims.claim: Christ is the way, the truth and the life.
claims.subject: Christ

claims.claim: The singer has been raised with Christ and has eternal life.
claims.subject: Union with Christ

claims.claim: The singer belongs to Christ and Christ to them.
claims.subject: Union with Christ

strengths.title: Takes Christ's own image and keeps its point
strengths.explanation: The vine and branches is about fruitlessness apart from him, and the song keeps that rather than softening abiding into a mood of closeness. The dependence is total and stated as such.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Apart from me you can do nothing — the claim the first verse states directly.

strengths.title: Quotes Christ's own self-description
strengths.explanation: Naming him the way, the truth and the life uses his words rather than a summary of them, and it settles the object of the song beyond doubt.
strengths.scriptureRationale: I am the way, and the truth, and the life.

strengths.title: Abiding grounded in an accomplished union
strengths.explanation: The song does not ask the singer to achieve closeness; it says they have been raised with Christ and belong to him already. Abiding follows from a fact rather than producing one.
strengths.scriptureRationale: If then you have been raised with Christ — the indicative that precedes the imperative.

strengths.title: Asks to be taught rather than assuming competence
strengths.explanation: The request is for instruction in abiding, which concedes that the singer does not know how. That humility is a small thing and it is the right posture.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Lord, teach us to pray — the disciples asking to be shown rather than assuming.

doctrinesAffirmed: Christ as the way, truth and life
Sanctification as taught rather than achieved
theological.assessment: A song about abiding that keeps the point of the image it borrows. The vine and branches is about fruitlessness apart from Christ, and the song states that rather than softening it into closeness. It quotes Christ's own self-description, and grounds the abiding in a union already accomplished rather than one the singer must produce. Nothing here needs correcting.

strengths.title: A chorus that grows as the song does
strengths.explanation: The chorus expands on each return rather than simply repeating, so the song develops without adding a bridge. A congregation follows the growth easily.

strengths.title: Carries without a band
strengths.explanation: Nothing depends on the arrangement. The song works on a piano or a guitar, which is the practical test of whether it belongs to the room.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Commonly published in C and D. Stepwise and modest in compass; a straightforward song for a mixed room.

range.key: Commonly published in C and D
range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The chorus returns three times and grows each time, so repetition adds material rather than sustaining a mood. Well judged for the length.
communal.assessment: Written for a congregation and undemanding to sing, with a chorus that develops rather than merely recurring. Its one communal shortfall is the singular voice, which sits oddly against an image about many branches on one vine.

strengths.title: One image, held throughout
strengths.explanation: The vine governs the whole song and never competes with a second metaphor. A hearer knows what is being pictured from the first verse to the last.

strengths.title: Christ named by his own words
strengths.explanation: Quoting the way, the truth and the life leaves no doubt who is being addressed, which many songs of intimacy fail to do.

clarity.assessment: Clear, single-minded and specifically addressed, pointing directly at the passage it draws from.

synthesis.summary: A song about abiding that keeps the point of the image it borrows: the vine and branches is about fruitlessness apart from Christ, and the song states that rather than softening it into closeness. It quotes Christ's own self-description and grounds the abiding in a union already accomplished rather than one the singer must produce.
